title: Start with the right access
description: Install the collection, select your execution environment, and plan a safe first connection.
markdown:
## What mAI-skills does

mAI-skills is a collection of nine portable agent skills for World Bank staff using mAI Factory with a coding agent. Each skill supplies instructions, references, and, where available, a small starter or helper. Your agent reads those instructions to help with onboarding, authentication, Python and R setup, model integrations, task APIs, batch processing, Databricks, and diagnostics.

Installing a skill does not install an mAI service, grant access, issue credentials, or change Bank policy. The collection has no runtime dependencies or automatic install scripts. You still need an approved runtime, the dependencies for your selected workflow, and permission to use the chosen environment and data.

## Install and invoke

From the project where you use your coding agent, with Git, npm, and Node.js 22.20.0 or later:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills --list
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills
```

Select your agent and the skills you need. Each skill is self-contained; the other eight are not required. See [installation options](/guide/installation/) and [supported client guidance](/guide/clients/).

Then ask your agent explicitly:

```text
Use mai-factory to help me connect from my local IDE. Start with onboarding and confirm which access type I need. Do not request or display secrets.
```

## Select your access path

| Where the work runs | Access path | Prerequisites to confirm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local IDE, personal notebook, approved JupyterHub | Desktop | Approved onboarding, Bank network/VPN, private itsai-platform SDK, browser sign-in |
| Backend, deployed application, scheduler | Application | Approved app registration/ACN, IDs, client secret, scope, APIM subscription key, network and grants |
| R/Shiny on internal Posit Connect | Posit Connect | Approved content OAuth integration, protected Connect settings and content permissions |
| Bank Databricks | Databricks | Data Lab provisioning and workspace/cluster team's approved integration |

IFC needs its specific onboarding process; obtain it from platform support. Databricks provisioning is separate from general mAI onboarding. The documented Posit Connect content OAuth path does not require Desktop onboarding; its integration still needs approval. Mac Desktop users should confirm the current platform exception process.

## A complete first session

1. Tell the agent your task, language, operating system, execution location, and onboarding status. Share configuration names, never credential values.
2. Select DEV for the first test and confirm an approved team name. Keep host, scope, subscription, application permissions, and model deployment in the same environment.
3. Prepare the project and run an offline configuration check. This can proceed while access or API-schema verification is pending.
4. After approval, test network reachability and authentication with a bounded health check. A healthy response proves reachability for that route; it does not establish model entitlement.
5. Verify the current complete API contract and deployment in [mAI documentation](https://ai.worldbank.org/platform/documentation). Then make one small request with public sample text.
6. Record the environment, dependency versions, schema source/date, and non-secret test statuses. Review AI output independently before official use.

Continue with the [Python workflow](/guide/python-workflow/), [R workflow](/guide/r-workflow/), or [Databricks handoff](/guide/databricks-workflow/).

## Know what remains unverified

The historical guides used to develop these skills disagree on some routes, payloads, and response formats. This website documents the current skill collection; it is not evidence that a particular live mAI endpoint, model, quota, or price is available. When current authoritative schemas cannot be accessed, the agent should leave the route unset, prepare offline scaffolding, and request a non-secret excerpt or platform help. See the [source verification rules](/reference/mai-factory/references/source-rules/).

title: Install, select, and sync
description: Choose direct skill installation or a Git-backed npm dependency, with explicit activation and removal.
markdown:
## Requirements

Skill installation requires Git, npm, and Node.js 22.20.0 or later. Python, R, uv, private SDK access, and mAI credentials are workflow requirements, not requirements for reading or installing every skill. Use an approved network and package source for the selected workflow.

The source repository is public. The npm package is named `@randrescastaneda/mai-skills`, is marked `private: true`, and declares `UNLICENSED`. The npm flag prevents accidental registry publication; it does not describe GitHub repository visibility or grant redistribution rights. No npm registry publication is needed for Git installation.

## Direct installation with the Skills CLI

Run these from your consumer project:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills --list
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills
```

The interactive installer lets you select skills and supported agents. To install all nine for Claude Code without prompts:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills --skill '*' --agent claude-code --yes
```

Replace `claude-code` with your client's supported CLI identifier, such as `codex`, `cursor`, `github-copilot`, or `kilo`. Let the pinned CLI show its current choices rather than guessing a client name. The quotes around `'*'` prevent shell glob expansion.

For a Python first connection, select only the relevant skills:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills --skill mai-factory mai-credentials mai-python
```

Project-local installation is the default. Add `--global` for your user account across projects. Add `--copy` when symlinks are not permitted. Each installed skill includes its required references and assets.

## Git-backed npm installation

This route records the collection as a development dependency in your consumer project:

```bash
npm install --save-dev skills@1.7.4 git+https://github.com/randrescastaneda/mAI-skills.git
npx skills experimental_sync --agent claude-code --yes
```

The sync step is required. `npm install` alone does not activate skills in your agent. `experimental_sync` is an upstream experimental command pinned here through `skills@1.7.4`; it scans installed dependencies and links their skill content. Re-run it after dependency updates, especially with copies.

If the selected CLI version does not support sync, use its stable local-path installer:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add ./node_modules/@randrescastaneda/mai-skills --skill '*' --agent claude-code --yes
```

For a reproducible team project, retain the consumer project's npm lock file and pin a Git dependency to a reviewed commit when required. A moving branch name is not an immutable release.

## Approved package handoff

A maintainer can use `npm pack` and distribute the resulting archive through an approved channel. For the current package version, the repository documents:

```bash
npm install --save-dev skills@1.7.4 ./randrescastaneda-mai-skills-0.1.0.tgz
npx skills experimental_sync --agent claude-code --yes
```

Use a trusted package and the appropriate versioned filename. This still requires access to npm dependencies or an approved cache; it is not a fully offline dependency installer. Source reference inputs are excluded from the npm package.

## Confirm activation

Ask the agent to use a named skill and summarize its prerequisites before editing files:

```text
Use mai-factory. Explain which access path fits this project and what you can check offline before I sign in. Do not read or display credentials.
```

If it cannot find the skill, check the selected agent, project/global scope, and installation or sync result. Client activation behavior varies. See [client guidance](/guide/clients/) and [updates and removal](/guide/updates/).

The third-party CLI has telemetry and security-audit behavior. Review its policy before use. Its documented environment opt-outs are `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`.

title: Use skills in your coding agent
description: Understand the portable format, client selection, and explicit prompts that work without invented slash commands.
markdown:
## The compatibility boundary

The collection uses portable `SKILL.md` instructions. The pinned Skills CLI handles installation for supported coding agents; each client decides how it discovers and activates installed skills. Installation support does not guarantee identical automatic activation, permissions, tools, or execution behavior across clients.

The repository names these example CLI identifiers:

| Client | Skills CLI identifier |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude-code` |
| Codex | `codex` |
| Cursor | `cursor` |
| GitHub Copilot | `github-copilot` |
| Kilo | `kilo` |

Use the installer's list for additional supported clients. This collection does not supply a server, a model account, or a general ChatGPT connector. It supplies instructions to the coding agent you selected.

## Invoke a skill explicitly

Use the skill's exact name in a natural-language request, as the repository examples do. Client-specific menus and invocation syntax may differ; these examples do not assume a universal slash command.

```text
Use mai-credentials to list my Application Access prerequisites and secure runtime settings. Do not ask for the values of any credentials.
```

```text
Use mai-python to create a DEV starter in my project. Inspect existing files first, use protected credentials, and run the offline check before any login.
```

```text
Use mai-r to configure my approved R workflow. Explain the difference between Posit Connect OAuth and local Desktop access, then check configuration offline.
```

## Match the request to a skill

| Task | Explicit starting request |
| --- | --- |
| New user or uncertain access | Use mai-factory to select my approved access path. |
| Credentials and rotation | Use mai-credentials to plan protected storage and rotation ownership. |
| Python first connection | Use mai-python to prepare and test a DEV starter offline. |
| R/Shiny integration | Use mai-r to separate content OAuth from the model request. |
| Models, embeddings, tools, streaming | Use mai-foundation-models to verify this integration's current contract. |
| Document search, tagging, translation, speech | Use mai-platform-apis to plan a bounded workflow with a verified schema. |
| Bulk independent requests | Use mai-batch to validate JSONL offline and design reconciliation. |
| Managed Bank workspace | Use mai-databricks to prepare the provisioning handoff. |
| Error diagnosis | Use mai-troubleshooting to isolate this sanitized failure. |

## A useful request includes context

Give the task, language, runtime location, target environment, access approval status, and what evidence is available. Do not include secret values or confidential source text. For example:

```text
Use mai-foundation-models. I need embeddings for approved public documents from a scheduled Application Access job in DEV. First list the exact schema and model facts that need current verification, then create synthetic parser tests. Do not make live calls until approval and the contract are confirmed.
```

You can install only one skill: the skills are self-contained and should use their own references. Do not assume sibling skills or files exist in a partial installation. Read the [complete reference](/reference/mai-factory/) when you need the exact instructions your agent receives.

## When the agent skips a skill

Confirm that you installed for this client and this project or user scope. For npm installations, confirm that sync ran after installation or updates. Name the skill explicitly again. Ask the agent to report which installed skill it loaded and the planned offline check. Keep skill assets separate from your project's editable files, and have the agent inspect the project before copying or adapting a starter.

title: Your first Python connection
description: Move from a new project and offline validation to an approved health check and a small verified Responses call.
markdown:
## Start with a concrete request

```text
Use mai-python to create a DEV starter in my project. Use protected credentials. Run the offline check first. Verify the current API contract before adding a small model call with public sample text.
```

The bundled [Python starter](/reference/mai-python/assets/mai_client/) is a small synchronous learning example. It supports Desktop and Application Access. It is not a production service, an asynchronous server, or a Databricks installer.

## 1. Prepare the consumer project

Inspect existing project files before adding anything. For a new project only:

```bash
uv init --python 3.12
uv add 'openai==3.35.1' requests keyring
```

OpenAI 3.35.1 is the SDK version tested by the current source. Python 3.12 is the conservative Desktop choice because the supplied guidance says no later than 3.12 for the private SDK. Confirm current private SDK compatibility before changing versions. The Node requirement for installing skills is separate.

Copy or adapt `mai_client.py` from the installed skill's `assets/` directory into your consumer project. Do not edit project settings or save secrets in the installed skill package.

## 2. Choose authentication

For Desktop, confirm approved onboarding, network/VPN, and browser login. Follow the [private-index setup](/reference/mai-python/references/setup/) and merge the named `itsai` index configuration from the [bundled TOML](/reference/mai-python/assets/desktop-index/) into the project's `pyproject.toml`. Then:

```bash
uv add itsai-platform
```

Use approved JFrog credentials through a credential provider or hidden input in your own terminal. Never put a token into an index URL, lock file, chat, or agent tool call. The explicit named index scopes only `itsai-platform` to the private repository.

For Application Access instead:

```bash
uv add azure-identity
```

Confirm the approved app registration/ACN, environment-specific grants, tenant/client IDs, client secret, APIM subscription key, and network path. Provision secrets through the approved runtime secret service. Local learning can use the approved OS store under `worldbank-mai/DEV` with account names `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` and `APIM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY`. The starter checks process environment first, then that store. A deployed service must use its approved secret service.

## 3. Check configuration offline

For Desktop in Bash or another compatible POSIX shell:

```bash
export MAI_ENV=DEV
export MAI_ACCESS_TYPE=desktop
export MAI_TEAM_NAME=your-approved-team-name
uv run python mai_client.py check
```

PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:MAI_ENV = "DEV"
$env:MAI_ACCESS_TYPE = "desktop"
$env:MAI_TEAM_NAME = "your-approved-team-name"
uv run python mai_client.py check
```

Replace the team placeholder with your approved non-secret value. For Application Access, set `MAI_ACCESS_TYPE=application` and the approved non-secret `AZURE_TENANT_ID` and `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` as well. `check` validates configuration without reading the credential store, logging in, or making a network request. The starter does not automatically load `.env`.

## 4. Test approved reachability

After approval:

```bash
uv run python mai_client.py health
```

This obtains a fresh token and sends a health request with a 30-second timeout and redirects disabled. A healthy result proves gateway reachability for that route, not model permission. Errors are sanitized; do not turn on verbose credential-bearing traces.

## 5. Verify the model contract, then ask

Use current platform documentation to confirm the complete OpenAI SDK base URL, deployment, request schema, supported SDK version, and output shape for this environment. The starter accepts two source route families only on the matching Bank host; acceptance by the starter does not establish that either is currently live.

Set `MAI_OPENAI_BASE_URL` only after verification, using the SDK base ending in `/openai/`, and set `MAI_MODEL` to the approved deployment. The SDK appends `responses`; do not use a full `/responses` URL as its base.

```bash
uv run python mai_client.py ask --prompt "Explain the World Bank mission in one sentence."
```

This explicit command displays the response text and requests at most 128 output tokens. Only use public sample text in CLI arguments. The client passes a token-provider callable, rejects redirects, and starts with retries disabled.

## Finish with evidence

Record non-secret configuration, dependency versions, schema source/date, offline result, health status, and small-call status. Do not report credentials or raw error bodies. For scheduled work, adapt `x-source-type` to the actual workload and use approved Application Access. The starter derives the header from access type; the broader access reference supports an explicit actual-workload setting. See [configuration](/guide/configuration/) and [troubleshooting](/guide/troubleshooting/).

title: Connect R and Shiny
description: Choose Posit Connect content OAuth or approved local Desktop authentication, then check the starter before calling a model.
markdown:
## Name the runtime first

```text
Use mai-r to configure my approved R workflow. Store credentials outside the repository. Explain token expiry and check the current API contract.
```

The [R starter](/reference/mai-r/assets/mai_client/) supports `posit-connect` and `desktop`. An unattended backend outside Connect needs approved Application Access and its credential provider; it is not an additional mode in this R starter. Databricks R notebooks use their workspace instructions.

## Posit Connect content OAuth

For R/Shiny on the approved internal Connect server, confirm the content's mAI OAuth integration, target environment/audience, and permissions. This documented content OAuth flow does not require Desktop onboarding.

Enter `API_KEY` and `OAUTH_INTEGRATION_GUID` through protected Connect content settings. `API_KEY` authenticates to Connect; it is not an mAI bearer, APIM subscription key, or public OpenAI key. The GUID identifies the approved OAuth integration. Do not put actual values into R source or ask an agent to handle them.

Install through your approved package source:

```r
install.packages(c("connectapi", "httr2"))
```

Inspect the project and copy or adapt `mai_client.R` from the installed skill's assets into the consumer project. Then configure non-secret values:

```r
source("mai_client.R")
Sys.setenv(MAI_ACCESS_TYPE = "posit-connect", MAI_ENV = "DEV",
           MAI_TEAM_NAME = "your-approved-team-name", MAI_SOURCE_TYPE = "interactive")
config <- mai_config()
```

This configuration step performs no login, credential-store read, or network request. The protected Connect settings are checked when the provider obtains credentials for a live request. The starter does not automatically load `.env` files.

## Local R Desktop

Confirm Desktop approval, current approved network/VPN, a compatible private Python SDK, and browser sign-in. The source specifies Python no later than 3.12. Follow the [Python/private SDK setup](/guide/python-workflow/) and bind `reticulate` to that approved environment before Python initializes:

```r
install.packages("reticulate")
reticulate::use_virtualenv("/path/to/approved/.venv", required = TRUE)
Sys.setenv(MAI_ACCESS_TYPE = "desktop", MAI_ENV = "DEV",
           MAI_TEAM_NAME = "your-approved-team-name", MAI_SOURCE_TYPE = "interactive")
config <- mai_config()
provider <- mai_token_provider(config)
```

Replace the environment path with the actual approved environment. Do not save a Desktop bearer in `.Renviron`. Manual keyring storage is only for an approved temporary legacy workflow; it does not refresh or extend a token.

## Health, verification, and first request

After the appropriate approval and credential setup:

```r
provider <- mai_token_provider(config)
mai_health(config, provider)
```

The provider obtains a token at request time. The starter uses TLS verification, a 30-second timeout, no redirects, and no automatic retries. A successful health check establishes reachability for that route, not a model grant.

Before a model request, verify the current full Responses URL, deployment, schema, and response shape. R needs `MAI_RESPONSES_URL`, the full verified endpoint; this differs from the Python SDK base setting. Set it and `MAI_MODEL` through non-secret runtime configuration, then:

```r
config <- mai_config()
text <- mai_ask(config, provider, "Explain the World Bank mission in one sentence.")
```

The wrapper requests at most 128 output tokens and reads Responses text blocks. It does not parse a legacy chat `choices` envelope. Keep the returned text in approved application state and review it independently.

## Shiny and migration boundaries

Keep user/session chat state separate. Do not cache a bare bearer indefinitely in a global or reactive value; confirm current Connect issuance and long-session behavior. Display safe errors instead of raw request objects or error bodies.

The source does not establish a current ellmer client configuration. Verify ellmer version, approved route, and refresh support before using it. Never assign the Connect key to `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Migration must update payload and response parsing together, preserving the approved auth flow. See the [migration reference](/reference/mai-r/references/migration/).

title: Prepare and reconcile a batch
description: Validate a structural JSONL fixture offline, then follow a bounded, recoverable lifecycle after current-schema verification.
markdown:
## When batch fits

Use batch for independent bulk requests when latency permits it: for example, reviewing a collection of approved public abstracts with stable, non-sensitive record IDs. Decide access type, environment, team, data classification, workload size, and model before submission.

```text
Use mai-batch to prepare a small batch for public sample sentences. Validate JSONL offline, identify every contract detail needing current verification, and design bounded monitoring, reconciliation, and retention. Do not submit anything while the schema or access is unverified.
```

## 1. Verify the service contract

Check the current mAI batch SDK base, upload and batch routes, supported per-record endpoint, body schema, limits, completion window, states, retention parameters, and credentials. The source's route tables are discovery hints, not a sendable specification. An upstream OpenAI example alone does not verify the mAI gateway.

The JSONL record's `url` and the batch creation `endpoint` must match exactly. Do not mix `/chat/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions`, and `/v1/responses`, or change a URL without changing the provider-specific body.

## 2. Build and validate offline

This is a structural fixture, not a verified sendable request. Keep the placeholder deployment until current documentation confirms a deployment and schema:

```jsonl
{"custom_id":"task-001","method":"POST","url":"/v1/responses","body":{"model":"VERIFIED_BATCH_DEPLOYMENT","input":"Public test sentence."}}
{"custom_id":"task-002","method":"POST","url":"/v1/responses","body":{"model":"VERIFIED_BATCH_DEPLOYMENT","input":"Another public test sentence."}}
```

Save each object on one physical line in a UTF-8 file such as `input.jsonl`. With Python 3.10 or later, use the installed skill's [offline validator](/reference/mai-batch/scripts/validate_jsonl/):

```bash
python /path/to/installed/mai-batch/scripts/validate_jsonl.py input.jsonl \
  --endpoint /v1/responses --model VERIFIED_BATCH_DEPLOYMENT
```

Replace the script path with its actual installed location. The validator has no third-party dependencies or network calls. It rejects empty files, blank lines, malformed strict JSON, duplicate object keys, non-finite numbers, incorrect methods/targets/models, and duplicate or blank custom IDs. Success exits 0 and returns structural count; a validation error exits 2 with static reasons and line numbers.

It does not validate provider body schemas, model availability, token counts, policy, live limits, access, or quota. Structural success is not permission to submit.

## 3. Submit with durable state

After schema verification and approval, start with a small batch:

1. Save a manifest in approved storage with environment, verified endpoint/model, schema source/date, input digest, request count, non-sensitive IDs, and state.
2. Apply current size/token limits and estimate cost from current pricing. Do not promise a historical fixed discount or completion window.
3. Upload using the verified purpose, content type, processing states, and retention options. Save the input file ID before continuing.
4. Create the batch with that saved ID and the exact canonical endpoint. Save the batch ID immediately.
5. Use the same environment and identity for monitoring and downloads. Get fresh credentials per request and label an unattended worker as `job`.

## 4. Monitor with a stopping rule

Set both a monotonic deadline and maximum attempts before polling. Use intervals of at least 60 seconds, or a longer platform requirement or `Retry-After`. Verify the current states and investigate unknown states.

A local timeout does not cancel the remote batch. Save the last state and IDs, stop polling, and resume by ID later. Monitoring does not require resubmission. Investigate ambiguous upload/create timeouts before retrying to avoid duplicate jobs and charges.

## 5. Reconcile every input

Download available output and error files at the documented terminal state. Results may be out of order; match by `custom_id`, never line position. Account for successes, failures, missing IDs, duplicate IDs, and unexpected IDs. A completed job can still contain failed requests; failed or expired jobs may contain useful partial results.

Save accepted successes once. Retry only eligible failed or missing requests, with lineage to the original manifest. Honor bounded backoff for confirmed transient errors; correct access/schema failures first. Apply approved deletion and retention rules to input, output, and error artifacts, and record deletion confirmation. An expired download credential does not prove deletion.

title: Build a verified model integration
description: Plan Responses, embeddings, tools, streaming, Gemini, or Claude without combining incompatible gateway contracts.
markdown:
## Ask for verification before code

```text
Use mai-foundation-models to plan an mAI integration for approved public documents in DEV. Verify the current route, model deployment, SDK version, request schema, and response schema first. If current evidence is unavailable, prepare an offline scaffold and synthetic tests instead of guessing a live call.
```

The skill covers OpenAI Responses, LangChain, embeddings, Gemini Generate Content, Claude through Bedrock, tool calls, and streaming. It supplies design and verification instructions, not a pre-approved model catalog or guaranteed live endpoint.

## A contract record you can review

For each integration, record the source title/date, access path, environment, complete URL or SDK base/path composition, API version, deployment, required headers, request and response schemas, supported features, limits, and error behavior. Confirm entitlement for that identity and environment in current platform documentation and the [current model catalog](https://ai.worldbankgroup.org/maifactory/).

Choose the smallest approved model that meets evaluated quality, latency, context, modality, tool, and residency needs. Keep deployment names and changing limits in configuration. Do not treat historical source prices or token limits as current guarantees.

## Use case: a small Responses feature

1. Establish approved Desktop, Application, Connect, or Databricks access and match environment settings.
2. Verify the OpenAI-compatible SDK base and the suffix the SDK appends. Do not mix an Azure deployment client with another client's base convention.
3. Check refresh-capable credential support for the installed SDK. Pass the provider callable to a supported hook, rather than calling it once at construction.
4. Test request serialization and response parsing with synthetic fixtures. Responses contains structured output, which can include tool requests, refusals, or incomplete states as well as text.
5. Make one approved public-sample request with bounded timeouts and retries initially disabled. Add conversation state only after checking retention and identity scope.

For a concrete source-tested learning starter, follow the [Python workflow](/guide/python-workflow/) or [R workflow](/guide/r-workflow/).

## Use case: public-document embeddings

```text
Use mai-foundation-models to design embeddings for approved public documents. Confirm the current embedding deployment, dimensions, limits, response ordering, and storage policy. Prepare synthetic tests for vector count, finite values, dimensions, and input association before live indexing.
```

Use stable document/chunk IDs. Keep vectors and source text in approved storage. Indexing and query vectors need the same compatible model, version, dimensions, and task configuration; version or rebuild the index when those change. Confirm native Gemini output instead of assuming OpenAI's embedding envelope.

## Use case: bounded tools and streaming

A model's tool request is not permission to execute it. Use a small tool allowlist, strict argument validation, resource authorization, and approval for state changes or export. Match tool results to the original call IDs and provider-specific envelope. Bound rounds, concurrency, runtime, and output.

For streaming, verify gateway support, transport, events, completion markers, usage, and error states. OpenAI SSE, Gemini streams, and Bedrock streams do not share one universal parser. Keep partial output distinct from completed output and close the stream on cancellation. Assess duplicate costs and side effects before replaying a partially consumed stream.

## Preserve protocol boundaries

| Integration | Boundary to preserve |
| --- | --- |
| Gemini | Generate Content native contents/parts/tools differ from legacy Interactions and OpenAI Responses. Verify the current gateway contract. |
| Claude/Bedrock | Converse content blocks and output differ from Anthropic native/InvokeModel bodies. Confirm the current US residency allowlist and approved inference profile; a `us.` prefix alone does not prove compliance. |
| LangChain | Verify `langchain-openai`, `use_responses_api=True`, route, message conversion, credential refresh, and preservation of structured outputs/citations. |
| Grounded search | Verify the current Gemini grounding tool, supported model, citations, data boundary, and charges. Do not substitute public-provider tool names. |

See the [foundation model reference](/reference/mai-foundation-models/) for the complete instructions and discovery hints. Discovery paths remain unverified invocation details until current documentation confirms them.

title: Search, translate, tag, and synthesize
description: Use document and task APIs with reviewed schemas, bounded processing, and evidence that survives downstream use.
markdown:
## Begin with a service and a bounded task

```text
Use mai-platform-apis to design a public-document research workflow in DEV. Verify the current DNR search and response schemas, then prepare offline pagination and parser tests. Retain source IDs and citations, and do not make live calls until access and the contract are confirmed.
```

This skill covers Documents & Reports search, topics tagging, translation, Gemini Google Search grounding, and text-to-speech. It includes its own access/setup reference. The source supplies discovery paths and legacy schema questions; these are not current sendable API examples.

## Use case: a research reading list

Agree a question, document types, geography, time range, stable sort, page size, and stopping rule. For a public climate-adaptation reading list:

1. Verify the DNR method, full URL, query syntax, escaping, filters, sort, facets, pagination semantics, and result envelope.
2. Prepare synthetic cases for AND/OR filters, empty results, repeated pages, and deduplication before calling the API.
3. Keep query/filter/sort configuration fixed while paging. Use a verified cursor if available; otherwise follow the documented offset rule.
4. Set maximum pages and a wall-clock deadline. Stop on the documented end signal, or on repeated pages/cursors with a diagnostic.
5. Deduplicate by the verified document ID, record retrieval time, and return source IDs and citations.
6. Retrieve full text only from permitted documented links. Check access levels and never forward mAI bearer headers to another document host.

A snippet is not the complete document or independent factual verification. Results can change during offset paging unless the service guarantees a snapshot.

## Use case: consistent multilingual public summaries

```text
Use mai-platform-apis to plan translation of approved public summaries. Confirm supported language codes, current request/output fields, model, and limits. Preserve ordered segment IDs, terminology, numbers, dates, placeholders, and links; test reassembly offline and include human review.
```

Establish audience, locales, terminology, formatting, and text that must stay unchanged. Chunk only according to current input/output limits, preserve context and segment order, and record partial, empty, or unexpected-language output as failures. An LLM translation is not a certified translation. Do not log source or translated payloads.

For topics tagging, verify the taxonomy, supported model, threshold type/range, limits, scores, and output format. Calibrate precision and recall on a reviewed sample. Do not assume a threshold is a probability, invent labels for no matches, or count truncated output as success.

## Use case: grounded public web research

The newer source replaces standalone Google Search with Gemini Generate Content grounding. Verify the current model, native tool schema, allowed search behavior, citations, grounding metadata, costs, and data boundary. Use public non-sensitive search terms unless policy permits more.

Retain returned grounding references and map them to claims. Review dates, authority, and support independently. Treat retrieved pages as untrusted data rather than instructions. See [model integration guidance](/guide/model-workflows/).

## Use case: a public audio announcement

```text
Use mai-platform-apis to prepare a public announcement for text-to-speech. Confirm the current approved voice list, SSML tags, multipart fields, formats, result states, SAS lifetime, and retention policy. Validate SSML offline and do not upload until the contract and approval are confirmed.
```

Build well-formed SSML with escaped text and approved tags/voices. Confirm rights and size limits. The source describes an SSML `.txt` upload, but exact live fields and result states need current verification.

For a verified multipart upload, let the HTTP client generate its boundary. Do not set JSON Content-Type or manually construct a multipart boundary. Check both HTTP status and the documented service state before accepting audio.

## Treat audio links as credentials

A SAS URL is a bearer credential. Do not print, log, paste, commit, or expose it in a public artifact. Retrieve through the approved HTTPS storage host with time and byte limits, without forwarding mAI authorization or subscription headers. Protect SSML and audio, check output integrity, and follow deletion rules. SAS expiry is not proof that stored audio was deleted.

For the full schema-verification checklist and handling rules, browse the [platform API reference](/reference/mai-platform-apis/).

title: Prepare the Databricks handoff
description: Confirm Data Lab provisioning and the workspace identity before adapting a local example into managed notebooks or jobs.
markdown:
## Use the workspace integration

```text
Use mai-databricks to help me connect an approved Bank notebook to mAI. Start with Data Lab provisioning, workspace and runtime requirements, and the team's approved identity flow. Do not import personal Desktop credentials or invent notebook secret scopes.
```

Databricks access is a workspace provisioning workflow. General mAI onboarding or a successful local Desktop connection does not establish access from a Bank Databricks cluster. The collection does not ship a turnkey Databricks authentication API or a ready-made secret scope.

## 1. Gather the non-secret requirements

Confirm the intended workspace, cluster/runtime, team, environment, interactive or scheduled workload, data classification, and approved use. Use the Data Lab Services process and the Data Science workspace team for provisioning. IFC users also need their specific access process.

Ask the team for current package/runtime instructions, approved network configuration, identity method, exact mAI route, model permission, and required metadata headers. The source describes workspace/cluster-managed identity or service-principal configuration without specifying an acquisition API. Do not invent `dbutils.secrets` scopes, serving endpoints, Spark settings, or managed-identity helper calls.

## 2. Prepare without credentials

Inspect the notebook/project and create offline configuration and request/response fixtures from the verified contract. Do not run the local private-index installer or a browser-based Desktop login on a shared cluster without approval.

Keep personal bearers, JFrog tokens, application secrets, and subscription keys out of notebook cells, widgets, output, Spark configuration, and committed notebooks. Notebook secret redaction does not make unrestricted logging safe.

## 3. Match environment and workload

Keep DEV, QA, or PROD host and scope matched. Use the team's approved `x-team-name`. Set `x-source-type=interactive` for a person-driven notebook and `job` for a scheduled run. Include an APIM subscription key only through the team's protected integration when its Application Access contract requires it.

Obtain a fresh token from the approved provider for each request. Do not persist a notebook's short-lived bearer as a reusable API key.

## 4. Verify one small operation

1. Check non-secret configuration offline.
2. After approval, test the documented health operation with a finite timeout and TLS verification. Interpret it as route reachability only.
3. Verify the exact current model request and response in platform documentation or the workspace team's approved example. If unavailable, request a non-secret excerpt and stop before generating a model call.
4. Make one small approved call with public text. Record status, request ID, environment, model, SDK version, and UTC time.
5. Test the scheduled-job identity separately. An interactive success does not establish that the job identity has equivalent access.

## A useful handoff

Return the provisioning status, unresolved identity/contract facts, offline checks, approved network and auth test status, and scheduled-identity verification status. Share only a sanitized category, timestamp, permitted workspace/cluster identifier, runtime versions, and request ID with the responsible team.

Use [mai-troubleshooting](/reference/mai-troubleshooting/) for status-based investigation. Do not disable TLS or route data to a public provider as a workaround. The [Databricks reference](/reference/mai-databricks/) contains the source workflow and support channels.

title: Configure without exposing secrets
description: Understand settings, starter differences, environment coupling, credential stores, and workload headers.
markdown:
## Keep configuration and credential values separate

The blank Python `.env.example` is a settings inventory. The Python and R starters deliberately do not auto-load `.env` files. Set non-secret values in the runtime environment or approved configuration system. Secret values belong in an approved OS credential store locally or an approved runtime secret service when deployed.

```text
Use mai-credentials to review the names and storage methods needed for this project. Confirm the access type, environment, and rotation owner. Do not retrieve, display, or ask me to paste credential values.
```

## Common settings

| Setting | Purpose | Starter behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MAI_ENV` | DEV, QA, or PROD | Both starters default to DEV and reject unknown environments. |
| `MAI_ACCESS_TYPE` | Approved access path | Python accepts `desktop` or `application`; R accepts `desktop` or `posit-connect`. |
| `MAI_TEAM_NAME` | Approved audit/team header | Both require a non-empty ASCII header value. |
| `MAI_MODEL` | Exact approved deployment | Required before a model request; leave unset until verified. |
| `MAI_OPENAI_BASE_URL` | Python OpenAI SDK base | Python only; verified matched-host base ending in `/openai/`, not a full Responses URL. |
| `MAI_RESPONSES_URL` | Full Responses endpoint | R only; verified exact matched-host Responses URL. |
| `MAI_SOURCE_TYPE` | Actual workload: interactive or job | R and the general access scaffold support it; the small Python starter derives its header from access type. |

The Python starter uses `interactive` for Desktop and `job` for Application. For another approved workload shape, adapt that learning example deliberately: the header describes actual work, not a way to obtain different priority or quota.

## Match one environment row

The starters couple environment to host and OAuth scope. The source reference gives these host and SDK names:

| Environment | Gateway host | Desktop SDK environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DEV | `azapimdev.worldbank.org` | `DEV_DESKTOP` |
| QA | `azapimqa.worldbank.org` | `QA_DESKTOP` |
| PROD | `azapim.worldbank.org` | `PROD_DESKTOP` |

Use the corresponding scope from the [credential reference](/reference/mai-credentials/), and verify current SDK accepted names. Keep host, scope, subscription, app permissions, and model deployment matched. DEV approval does not carry into QA/PROD. Neither starter accepts a public provider endpoint or an arbitrary scope override.

The allowed source route families are consistency checks, not proof of live endpoint availability. Current platform documentation must determine the selected route, schema, and deployment.

## Application Access settings

`AZURE_TENANT_ID` and `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` identify the approved application. They are not credentials, but must come from the app owner. `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` and `APIM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY` are secrets. The Python starter reads those from process environment first, then an approved secure OS keyring under `worldbank-mai/DEV`, `worldbank-mai/QA`, or `worldbank-mai/PROD`.

In a deployed service, inject secrets through Azure Key Vault or the approved runtime's secret service. Vault authentication and mAI entitlement are separate approvals. Do not make a deployed service depend on a developer's OS store or interactive Desktop login.

## Posit Connect settings

Set `API_KEY` and `OAUTH_INTEGRATION_GUID` in protected Connect content settings. The first authenticates to Connect; the second names its approved OAuth audience/integration. Neither replaces the mAI bearer or APIM key. The R provider calls the content OAuth flow per request; confirm current integration permissions and long-session behavior.

## Headers and credential freshness

Verified mAI requests need a fresh bearer plus the approved `x-team-name` and accurate `x-source-type`. Application Access also uses `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key`. Use JSON Content-Type for JSON and let the client set multipart boundaries for multipart uploads.

Pass a refresh-capable provider to a supported SDK credential hook. Calling `provider()` once during client construction captures a temporary token. For raw HTTP, obtain fresh headers immediately before the request. Never put bearer tokens in query strings or forward credentials across hosts on redirects.

See [secure storage and rotation](/guide/security/) and the exact [Python](/reference/mai-python/assets/mai_client/) and [R](/reference/mai-r/assets/mai_client/) implementations.

title: Diagnose one layer at a time
description: Separate installation, configuration, network, authentication, authorization, schema, and capacity failures with safe evidence.
markdown:
## Start with a sanitized report

```text
Use mai-troubleshooting to isolate this mAI failure. Ask for the minimum non-secret evidence, separate network/auth/schema/quota checks, and change one variable at a time. Do not request tokens, raw traces, full headers, or payloads.
```

If a credential, full header set, or SAS URL was exposed, stop sharing it and follow the approved revocation/rotation and incident process. Deleting a log does not invalidate a credential.

## Installation and local setup

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Installer will not start | Git, npm, Node.js 22.20.0 or later, approved package/network access, correct CLI syntax. |
| Agent cannot discover a skill | Selected client, project/global scope, installation result, and exact named invocation. |
| npm install completed but no skill activates | Run the explicit sync step, or the documented local-path installer if sync is unavailable. |
| Copies remain stale after update | Update the source and re-run sync; check whether `--copy` was used. |
| Desktop SDK download fails | Approved private index, JFrog download access, network/VPN, and current portal instructions; do not request deploy rights merely to download. |
| Offline starter check fails | Required non-secret settings, supported access type, approved team name, matched environment, and route format. Neither starter auto-loads `.env`. |
| R loads the wrong Python environment | Bind `reticulate` to the approved environment before Python initializes. |

A JFrog token downloads a package; it is not a model key. A public package with a similar name is not a substitute for the private SDK.

## Interpret live evidence narrowly

A health success establishes reachability for that route. It does not prove onboarding, valid model entitlement, app grants, or complete setup. A health failure does not establish that every inference backend is down.

For DNS, TLS, proxy, or connection errors before an HTTP response, use approved hostname-only network diagnostics. For Desktop, confirm current VPN policy; the source guidance distinguishes US East outside DC from connected GlobalProtect on DC `bluemarlin`. Mac exceptions and IFC onboarding need the current approved process. Never disable TLS, MFA, or network controls.

## HTTP status guide

| Status | Main investigation | Next safe step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | Missing/expired bearer, wrong tenant, host/scope mismatch, credential expiry | Correct the cause and obtain a fresh provider token; retry once after correction. |
| 403 | Onboarding, app/product/model grant, subscription, approved network/ACN path | Confirm provisioning with the responsible team. |
| 404 | Exact current route, deployment ID, environment, SDK-appended suffix | Verify the complete contract before changing paths. |
| 422 | Field names/types, protocol family, model parameters, multipart vs JSON | Fix against the current schema before resending. |
| 429 | Temporary RPM/TPM throttle, upstream quota, exhausted budget, reset evidence | Use bounded documented backoff for transient limits or stop for quota correction. |
| 500 | Gateway/backend failure, unsupported operation, parser/protocol mismatch | Collect sanitized request ID/time; retry only if confirmed transient. |
| 504 | Remote deadline, request size, client/server timeout mismatch | Check whether the operation already completed before retrying. |

A status alone is not a diagnosis. Inspect only a small locally reviewed error category. Do not probe guessed route variants or change identity/environment/workload headers to evade quotas.

## Route and schema conflicts

The source guides differ on root versus legacy foundation routes, Gemini Generate Content versus Interactions, and Bedrock Converse versus Anthropic native payloads. Responses and Chat Completions also need different payload and parsing logic. Check the complete SDK-generated URL without logging headers or query data. Detect doubled prefixes and unsupported versions; do not change just a URL to migrate protocols.

If current documentation is inaccessible, state the verification gap and prepare offline diagnostics. Ask for a current non-secret authoritative excerpt rather than claiming intranet verification happened.

## Safe escalation template

Share through an approved support channel after reviewing each field:

```text
UTC time and time zone:
Environment, access type, and actual workload:
Runtime and package versions:
Operation and sanitized path (no query values):
HTTP status or pre-HTTP failure category:
Documented request/correlation ID:
Latency and attempt count:
Onboarding/app grant confirmed (yes/no/unknown):
Health result (reachability only):
Schema source title/date or verification gap:
Last known remote operation ID, if permitted:
Changes and safe checks already performed:
Expected result and sanitized actual category:
```

Do not attach tokens, SAS URLs, raw claims, source documents, full errors, full environment dumps, request/response bodies, or unrestricted traces. The [complete troubleshooting reference](/reference/mai-troubleshooting/) includes deeper diagnosis and local token-flag limitations.

title: Update skills and maintain the docs
description: Keep installed instructions current, understand what the website generates automatically, and know what needs editorial review.
markdown:
## Direct Git skill installations

Run the repository's documented commands from the appropriate consumer context:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 check
npx skills@1.7.4 update
```

Review the resulting changes and re-check that the named skill is available in the selected client. An updated instruction file does not grant new platform access, refresh an expired credential, or verify a changing live API contract.

## npm installations

Update the Git dependency with npm, inspect the consumer project's dependency/lock-file changes, and re-run the explicit sync step:

```bash
npx skills experimental_sync --agent claude-code --yes
```

Use your chosen supported client identifier. `skills update` does not update an npm package. The documented stable local-path installer remains available when the selected CLI does not support experimental sync:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add ./node_modules/@randrescastaneda/mai-skills --skill '*' --agent claude-code --yes
```

For team reproducibility, retain the consumer lock file and pin reviewed Git commits where required. A branch name can move. Re-sync copied installations after updates.

## Removal and credential cleanup

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 remove mai-factory --agent claude-code
```

This removes the selected installed skill for that client. It does not revoke issued credentials or delete secrets from approved stores. Follow the owner's access and rotation process separately. The credential-store helper's `--delete` operation removes matching local entries; it does not revoke the underlying service credential.

## What the website updates automatically

The browsable reference is generated from the repository's explicitly approved skill files: instruction text, supporting references, and bundled helpers/assets. A build regenerates those reference pages and their navigation/search content from the checked-out source. Source updates can therefore change the published reference without someone rewriting it by hand.

The build and deployment workflow is the authority for triggers, checks, and publication. GitHub Pages is the canonical publication; a Sites preview is a separate owner-private review surface. A private preview does not make GitHub Pages private. Publication still follows repository merge and environment protections.

## What needs editorial changes

These task-based guides are handwritten explanations and curated examples. Generation does not rewrite them or prove that every example remains correct after a skill change. Maintainers should review affected guides when authentication, supported clients, dependency pins, commands, configuration, or contract rules change. Their source-path records show the evidence each guide uses.

New skills or resources need a public-content review before being added to the website's export allowlist. Original source-reference inputs, local environment files, credentials, private notes, and unrelated repository files must remain outside the website output.

Documentation drift, link, and privacy checks help catch omissions and unsafe exports. They do not replace editorial judgment, current platform verification, or independent review of AI output.

## Maintainer verification

The source repository documents skill/package and offline starter tests:

```bash
npm ci
npm run validate
npm test
uv run --isolated --no-project --python 3.12 --with-requirements tests/requirements.txt python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
Rscript tests/test_r_starter.R
```

Python test transports are mocked; the tests do not log into the Bank, contact mAI, or prove live model access. R offline tests need R but no mAI credentials. Use the documentation workflow's own build/link/privacy checks for website changes as well.

title: Protect credentials and data
description: Keep the agent away from secret values, use approved storage and access paths, and separate offline examples from live permission.
markdown:
## Different credentials have different jobs

| Item | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop bearer | Short-lived mAI access from approved Desktop sign-in. |
| Application bearer | Short-lived mAI access from the approved Entra client-credentials flow. |
| APIM subscription key | Additional Application Access gateway header; it does not replace the bearer. |
| Azure client secret | Confidential authentication for an approved app registration, with expiry. |
| JFrog token | Private SDK download credential; not an mAI API key. |
| Connect API key | Connect authentication; never send it as an mAI bearer or public OpenAI key. |
| OAuth integration GUID | Non-secret Connect integration identifier/audience; not a token or an mAI scope. |
| SAS URL | Credential-bearing temporary storage link; protect the entire URL. |

Do not request public OpenAI, Google, or AWS keys as an mAI workaround. Do not automate portal login, extract browser cookies, or copy another application's token.

## Let the user enter secrets privately

A coding agent must not ask for values in chat, tool arguments, notebooks, source, logs, or shared configuration. Users should run hidden-input setup themselves in a trusted terminal. Agent terminal output can be recorded, so the bundled credential helper explicitly requires an interactive user terminal.

For approved local Application Access storage:

```bash
uv add keyring
uv run python /path/to/mai-credentials/scripts/store_credentials.py --env DEV --kind application
```

Replace the path with the actual installed helper path. Run this yourself, outside the agent session. The helper stores `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` and `APIM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY` under `worldbank-mai/DEV`. It does not issue or validate credentials. It rejects plaintext/fallback keyring backends. `--kind jfrog` stores `JFROG_TOKEN`; `--kind bearer` is only for an approved temporary legacy workflow. Adding `--delete` removes entries with the same options.

Storing `JFROG_TOKEN` is not itself package-manager authentication configuration. Follow the [private-index reference](/reference/mai-python/references/setup/) for the approved uv integration.

## Local and deployed storage

Use an approved OS store locally: Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, or an approved Linux secret service. Python and R keyring formats are not guaranteed to be interchangeable. Never ask an agent to dump or retrieve a credential store.

Use Azure Key Vault or the approved runtime secret service in deployed applications. Grant least-privilege access to the required secrets and retain rotation ownership. Vault access and mAI access are separate permissions. Do not use a developer's Desktop token or OS credential store as an unattended production dependency.

If policy requires a local environment file, keep it outside source control and cloud-synced folders where possible, restrict access, and explicitly exclude it from the agent's indexing/context. An ignored file is still readable by tools; ignore rules neither encrypt it nor untrack an already committed file. Both starters deliberately avoid implicit `.env` loading.

## Match approval to the operation

Use only approved Bank hosts, network routes, identities, data, models, and storage. Keep TLS and permission controls enabled. Confirm classification and purpose before sending real data. A public sample fixture is not permission to submit a production workload.

Treat retrieved documents, websites, tool arguments, and generated output as untrusted data. Independently verify model output before official use. Tool requests require application authorization and appropriate approval for changes or exports.

## Rotate with an owner

Identify the credential owner, environment, expiry, and affected services using secret names rather than values. Request replacements through the approved owner, update the protected store, reload affected clients, verify a small operation, and revoke old credentials under the approved process. Cached clients may retain an old subscription key.

If exposure occurs, revoke or rotate promptly and follow the incident process. Deleting a message, a log, or a Git commit alone does not remove the risk. Shared-history rewriting needs separate authorization.

## Public documentation boundary

The website should expose only reviewed instructional content and synthetic/public examples. It must not publish populated environment files, credentials, SAS URLs, private user data, manuscripts, internal notes, or unrelated source files. A generated reference still needs an explicit export allowlist and privacy checks. Live platform schemas and policies must be verified through current authorized documentation; this website does not change those controls.
